glosses: to reach a solution or an end through fighting; to fight it out

examples.text:
1799, Samuel Richardson, Geschiedenis van Karel Grandison (= tr. of The History of Sir Charles Grandison), part 4, Johannes Allart (publ.), pages 314 and 315.
Wel, en meent gij niet, dat wij elkander aankeeken, als een paar zotten, toen wij alleen zagen, opdat wij, om zoo te ſpreken, den ſtrijd zouden uitvechten?
examples.translation: Well, and you don't suppose that we were looking at one another like a pair of fools, when we were only watching, so that we, so to speak, would fight out the battle?
examples.english: Well, and you don't suppose that we were looking at one another like a pair of fools, when we were only watching, so that we, so to speak, would fight out the battle?

examples.text: Onze kennis ervan is zeer beperkt en ook vervalst door de propaganda-oorlogen die de koloniale machten met elkaar uitvochten.
examples.translation: Our knowledge about it is seriously limited and also falsified by the propaganda wars that the colonial powers fought out with each other.
examples.english: Our knowledge about it is seriously limited and also falsified by the propaganda wars that the colonial powers fought out with each other.
